claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you tell me: **How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm inquiring about my child. His name is Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're inquiring about your child Alex.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to gather some details about your circumstances. Let me start with this:

**What is Alex's date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 8 years old - he was born in 2016.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. So Alex was born in 2016 and is currently 8 years old.

**Are you Alex's parent or guardian, and do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm his parent and I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that.

**Is Alex in full-time education or training, or does he have any disabilities or health conditions that we should be aware of?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 8, so he's in primary school. No disabilities or health conditions that affect his eligibility - he's a healthy kid.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know. Thank you.

**Are you currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex, or would this be a new claim?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: This would be a new claim - I'm not currently receiving it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know.

**What is your current residency status in the UK? For example, are you a British citizen, settled status holder, or do you have another immigration status?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for that information.

**Do you have parental responsibility for Alex, and does he live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have parental responsibility and he lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. That's very helpful.

**In the last 3 months, have you or Alex been away from the UK for more than 4 weeks at a time?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, we've both been here in the UK the whole time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

**Are there any other children living with you that you might also want to claim Child Benefit for, or is Alex your only child?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is my only child.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 8 years old (born in 2016)
- You are his parent with parental responsibility
- He lives with you in the UK
- You are a British citizen residing in the UK
- You've both remained in the UK
- This is a new claim

Let me provide you with my eligibility assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Congratulations! You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

All the key eligibility requirements are satisfied:
- ✓ Alex is under 16 years old
- ✓ You have parental responsibility and he lives with you
- ✓ You are a British citizen with the right to reside in the UK
- ✓ There are no disqualifying circumstances

You can now proceed with making your claim for Child Benefit. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
